# BetterNCM - Plugin Library

This repo is the plugin library for BetterNCM.

## Plugin Submission and Updates

0. Confirm that your plugin complies with the [listing guidelines](https://github.com/MicroCBer/BetterNCM/wiki/%E6%8F%92%E4%BB%B6%E5%95%86%E5%BA%97%E4%B8%8A%E6%9E%B6%E6%8F%92%E4%BB%B6%E6%96%B9%E5%BC%8F%E5%8F%8A%E5%87%86%E5%88%99#%E4%B8%8A%E6%9E%B6%E5%87%86%E5%88%99)
1. Fork this repository
2. Create a JSON file in the `plugins-list` directory with the following content

```js
{
    "name": "ExamplePlugin", // Plugin name
    "repo": "BetterNCM/example-plugin", // Plugin's repo
    "branch": "main", // Branch name
    "subpath": "/", // Subdirectory of the plugin within the repo (optional)
    "author": "Author" // Author
}
```

3. Submit a PR
4. The script periodically fetches the version number from the plugin's Manifest and automatically submits updates and review requests. You can also send `update` in the QQ group to manually trigger the fetch script.
5.

## Notes

+ Make sure the plugin directory being synced to this repository contains no extra files (other than files required to run the plugin and the plugin preview image).
+ Alternatively, create a .betterncm-ignore file to filter out unneeded files (format similar to .gitignore).
+ Compress preview images and make sure they are not too large
+ Native plugins must be compiled using GitHub Actions.

## Manifest.json Format

```js
{
    "$schema": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BetterNCM/BetterNCM-Plugins/refs/heads/master/manifest-schema.json",
    "manifest_version": 1, // Manifest version, must be 1
    "name": "ExamplePlugin", // Plugin name
    "slug": "example-plugin", // Unique plugin identifier (English letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores) (leave empty to auto-generate from the plugin name) (fill in this field if the plugin name contains Chinese characters)
    "fork_of": "example-plugin-origin", // If this is a variant/fork of another plugin, this marks the slug of the source plugin
    "version":…

Buwrt/githup.body:
# githup

A third-party GitHub client for Android. The `hup` in the name is **hub**, the GitHub you carry in your pocket.

Technically it's a bit interesting: **a WebView hosts a pure front-end single-page app, and the native layer only handles what the web can't do**, such as network requests that bypass cross-origin restrictions, the system file picker, binary uploads, and downloading and launching the installer. So the whole thing is compressed to **around 350 KB**, yet it covers browsing repositories, viewing Issues / PRs, checking Actions, publishing Releases, uploading files, and even having GitHub Actions in the cloud build an APK for you.

What each version changed is recorded in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/Buwrt/githup/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md) (starting from v1.1.3).

The moment the app opens, it automatically checks this repository to see whether it's the latest version. **If it's already the latest, it stays completely silent with no reaction at all. Only when a new version exists does it remind you, according to version-number rules.** You can also publish a new build without changing the version number: upload the new package and update the checksum, and users will get a prompt the next time they open the app. The comparison is based on the installer package fingerprint, not just the version number. For details, see [Update mechanism](https://github.com/Buwrt/githup#更新机制).

> This app is a third-party client for personal learning purposes and is not affiliated with GitHub, Inc. All data is obtained through GitHub's official public API, and access tokens are stored only on your device.

EmberCollective/CampusRunning.description: Campus Running (keep) one-click solution tool. Supports custom pace adjustment, generating historical data, custom track configuration, and multiple batch generation modes. Ready to use out of the box, no complex deployment required.
EmberCollective/CampusRunning.body:
> **Disclaimer**: This project is provided solely for learning, exchange, and technical research. Please voluntarily abide by the relevant rules of your school and the sports platform. All consequences arising from the use of this tool are borne by the user.

## Campus running has been a long ordeal

Early check-ins, mileage and pace, none of it can be skipped. Students have suffered from it for a long time.

The community already has many virtual location solutions, each with its own trade-offs. This tool takes a different path: **it generates sports data files (FIT by default, TCX-compatible) with real track coordinates, real pace, and real cadence and step counts. Import them into a sports app and they are ready to use.**

The author maintains this project out of passion and hopes to help students struggling with campus running everywhere. If this project has helped you, starring it is the best encouragement the author can receive.

## What it can do

Four generation modes, covering everything from "backfill a single record" to "complete a whole semester at once":

| Mode | Command | Use case |
|------|---------|----------|
| Daily range | `daily` | Given a date range, randomly generates a distance within a kilometer range each day |
| Total kilometers | `total` | Given a total distance, automatically distributes it across days (weekends can be 1.5× weekdays, with support for weekly rest days) |
| Single file | `single` | Backfills one record with a specified distance for a particular date |
| Batch by specified dates | Web only | Select any combination of dates on a calendar and batch-generate them day by day |

Each record gets its "realism" from five layers of mechanisms:

- **Real track**: Generates clockwise GPS track points based on track coordinates. Multiple campus tracks are built in, and you can add your own.
- **Real pace**: Four-stage pace fluctuation (warm-up, steady, fatigue, sprint), rejecting uniform straight-line motion.
- **Real cadence and steps**: Generates cadence curves that follow a realistic distribution based on pace and distance, written to both FIT and TCX.
- **Coordinate correction**: Automatically corrects the systematic GCJ-02 offset so the track lands where it should.
- **Visual track editor**: In the web UI, plot points on an AMap map to draw a track, then save it as a config with one click.

The CLI and web entry points produce consistent results.

## Quick start

### Desktop version (recommended, ready to use)

**No Python environment required.** Download from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/YuShenLiu06/CampusRunning/releases) and use it directly:

| Platform | Download file | Notes |
|----------|---------------|-------|
| Windows | `CampusRunningGen-Setup-<version>-win64.exe` | Installer (recommended) or portable zip |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `CampusRunningGen-<version>-macos-arm64.zip` | Unzip and use |

Functionality is fully identical to the web version. System requirements, SmartScreen / Gatekeeper…

## iOS App Maintenance

Free Apple ID signing typically expires after 7 days. When the app won't open after expiration, reconnect the iPhone and press `Cmd + R` in Xcode to reinstall and renew the signing for 7 more days:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22
npx cap open ios
```

If you're only renewing the signing without changing content, you don't need to rebuild the web artifacts.

If you've modified the blog content, you need to rebuild and sync first:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 16.19.1
MOBILE=1 npm run docs:build

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22.22.2
npx cap sync ios
npx cap open ios

chinjiaqing/jc-daily-report.body:
# ⚽ Football Signal Radar · Daily Signal Report

> **Set emotion aside, watch only the signals.**
> Cross-validation of odds movements across three channels; no bets on low odds, no bets when signals are unclear. Pre-match execution is automatic, and post-match settlement is automatic.

## 🚀 Online Site

- **[https://chinjiaqing.github.io/jc-daily-report/](https://chinjiaqing.github.io/jc-daily-report/)**
- Updated automatically every hour, with historical dates archived for review at any time
- Covers **500–1300+** matches per day (full Sporttery / Asian handicap coverage), with signals and bets automatically flagged

---

## The Detours We Bypassed

We tried **models**: we piled up parameters until the room was full. Looking back, the model was just repeating prices the market had already set, and no amount of extra parameters could produce anything new.

We tried **studying the bookmakers**: guessing at the house's tactics, guessing again, and growing more paranoid with every guess. In the end the realization was that guessing at the bookmaker is less useful than watching the price.

We also tried **AI prediction**: injuries, motivation, form. Each point sounded convincing, and each had already been priced into the odds long before. However loud the talk, the handicap does not agree.

After the detours, one plain principle remains:

> **Money shows where it is going, and the handicap speaks.**
> But people watching the lines get carried away easily: chasing favorites, fearing upsets, and shaking under pressure. It is easy to see that emotion is driving the trade.

So we hand both the "watching" and the "buying" to the machine, and keep only one thing for the human: **discipline**.

## Three Informants, One Referee

**1X2 (European odds)** tracks market-wide odds movements: who has been collectively abandoned, who is quietly defending, and whether the draw line has been given up. This is the informant closest to the action.

**Asian handicap** tracks the handicap line and water (odds): sudden pivots near kickoff, and snipes on the favored side. Money is being thrown down in real cash, which is more reliable than anything said out loud.

**Over/Under** tracks the total goals line: when a breeding ground for goals appears, the number of goals in the match has often already been decided.

Each of the three informants has its own information. When the information agrees, the referee is willing to make a call. **Matches where the signals don't agree (European odds and Asian handicap contradicting each other) are not touched at all.** When the informants are arguing among themselves, there is no reason for you to place a bet.

## Discipline Matters More Than Vision

Once the direction is set, everything else is discipline:

- **No bets on low odds**: single-selection odds below 1.5, or double-selection odds that work out below 1.3, are not bought no matter how good the signal looks. At odds that low, even a win does not make much money.
- **No bets when the signal is unclear**: no signal, conflicting signals, or ambiguous direction means waiting. Missing a bet costs nothing; a bad bet loses money.
- **Quality determines stake size**: the stronger the signal, the larger the stake (1/2/4 units). No all-in gambling.
- **Automatic betting 15 minutes before kickoff, automatic settlement once results come in**: no last-minute shakiness, no urge to raise the stake after a win or to chase losses after a loss.

---

## ⚠️ Disclaimer

This project is for data research only and does not constitute any purchase advice. Buy lottery tickets only at licensed physical retail outlets. Persons under 18 years of age may not participate.

dragonstaryuri-sys/evolia.body:
# Evolia 🌿

> **“We are not born complete; we keep evolving into a better version of ourselves through collisions with the world.”**

Evolia is an in-depth AI companion app focused on “personal growth” and “emotional resonance.” This project is a derivative of [LastChat](https://github.com/RikkaHub/LastChat). While keeping LastChat's powerful AI integration capabilities, it substantially restructures the memory system and interaction, and adds features such as schedule management and automated tasks.

---
## 🧠 Core Features

### 1. Deeply Evolving Memory System (L0-L3 Hierarchy)
We designed a rigorous memory hierarchy so the AI understands you better than you understand yourself:
- **L0: Immediate context**: a sliding window that captures the thread of the current conversation.
- **L1: Rolling summary (Context Refresh)**: automatically compresses past conversation, preserving long-term context while saving tokens.
- **L2: All-day episodic memory (Episodic Memory)**: maintains coherence across multiple conversation windows, giving the AI round-the-clock timeline awareness.
- **L3: Master Memory**: automatically synced at dawn, settling lasting memories about “promises” and the “current state of the relationship.”

### 2. Smart Retrieval and Reranking (RAG Optimization) 🆕
To ensure the memories the AI retrieves are both precise and relevant, we implemented an efficient two-stage retrieval mechanism:
- **Two-stage filtering**: a first-stage “broad recall” ensures coverage (recalling 3× the configured count), and a second-stage “strict re-ranking” uses a reranking model for the final relevance check.
- **Hybrid scoring engine**: supports mixed matching of vector semantics (Semantic) and keywords (Keyword), and introduces a **Recency Boost** weight to prioritize recently occurring memories.
- **Hard threshold gate**: strictly enforces the “composite score threshold” filter. After reranking, interfering information that falls below the threshold is not sent into the AI context, eliminating irrelevant memory noise.

### 3. User Watcher and System Control (The Watcher)
Evolia's AI no longer just passively waits for replies; it has gained the ability to “perceive” and “act”:
- **Phone state observer (Peek User)**: high-precision monitoring of the foreground app, usage duration (including single-session duration statistics), on-screen text context, and recent tap actions.
- **Proactive intervention triggers**: the AI can set complex monitoring tasks (e.g., scrolling Douyin for over 30 minutes, still being on the phone late at night) and proactively trigger reminders through hidden instructions.

leizongmin/ZeroWeb.body:
# ZeroWeb

ZeroWeb is an experimental cross-platform browser project written in Rust. This repository is working on two things at once:

Website: [zeroweb.leizm.com](https://zeroweb.leizm.com)

- An embeddable, reusable `ZeroWebView` library
- A complete `ZeroBrowser` browser application

The project aims to keep the core code and dependency boundaries in its own hands, so the page engine is being built gradually on top of permissively licensed Rust components. The DOM, CSS, layout, rendering, navigation, and security boundaries are all being built out layer by layer in this repository.

This is also an AI-first engineering experiment: humans are responsible only for solution design, key decisions, and result verification, while nearly all code development is done autonomously by AI. We want to see how far AI can advance a complex system like this when architectural boundaries, tests, and acceptance criteria are clearly defined.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This repository is still experimental, mainly used for learning, research, and engineering exploration. The core crates and tests already have a fair amount, but the browser shell, a complete page JavaScript runtime, and real-site compatibility are still on the way. It is not currently a browser usable for daily work. For commercial or other production use, please evaluate features, security, compatibility, performance, and license-boundary risks yourself.

**Quick navigation**

- [Roadmap](https://github.com/leizongmin/ZeroWeb/blob/HEAD/ROADMAP.md)
- [Website](https://zeroweb.leizm.com)
- [Current status](#当前状态)
- [Quick start](#快速开始)
- [Repository structure](#仓库结构)
- [Documentation navigation](#文档导航)
- [Contributing](#参与贡献)
- [License](#许可证)

## Project positioning

- **Embedding first**: Besides the browser app, the project will also deliver a stable Rust `ZeroWebView` API so other applications can integrate it directly.
- **License boundaries first**: Mainline dependencies preferentially use permissive licenses such as MIT, Apache-2.0, and BSD, to avoid core capabilities being constrained by unsuitable copyleft dependencies.
- **Full-stack Rust route**: The page engine, host layer, and rendering infrastructure are all kept within the Rust ecosystem as much as possible.
- **AI can write, but it must be reviewable**: AI-assisted contributions are welcome, but submitted changes must be explainable, well tested, and clearly reviewable.

# HoloCard

Chinese | [English](https://github.com/longsizhuo/holocard/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

HoloCard automatically splits a photo into layers and renders it as an interactive holographic card. The server estimates the photo's depth and divides it into several foreground, midground, and background layers, each with its own independent foil surface. The card rotates with the pointer or with device tilt. Live site: https://holocard.longsizhuo.com

The foil effect and interaction feel are ported from [pokemon-cards-css](https://github.com/simeydotme/pokemon-cards-css) (Simon Goellner, GPL-3.0). That project requires hand-drawn foil masks for each card. HoloCard uses a layering algorithm to generate the masks automatically, so any photo can be turned into a card.

Please report issues in this repository, not to the upstream project. > > **The project is in public Beta.** The officially supported scope is **trusted LAN**. When away from home, prefer Tailscale (zero-server, direct connection); the relay (DLP/1) is a no-configuration fallback and remains experimental. The plugin, App, and sync protocol iterate quickly, so before upgrading, see [`CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/lunaship/dsh-cetus/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md) and the [compatibility matrix](https://github.com/lunaship/dsh-cetus/blob/HEAD/docs/COMPATIBILITY.md). ## Remote Connection When the computer and phone are on the same Tailscale network, the pairing QR code automatically includes the Tailscale address. The phone first tries the primary LAN address, then this direct connection if it is unreachable, and uses the relay only if both fail. You don't need to enter a `100.x` address yourself, nor run a separate server. The relay is a no-configuration fallback for when Tailscale isn't installed. Details are in [`REMOTE_ACCESS.md`](https://github.com/lunaship/dsh-cetus/blob/HEAD/REMOTE_ACCESS.md). --- ## Push Gateway (DLPUSH/1) iOS doesn't allow persistent SSE in the background, so once the phone leaves the App there is no connection; the push gateway fills this gap. operator                          # interactive TUI
